questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and other vehicles?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: What is hardest to see at night?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: After an emergency vehicle with its siren on passes you, what must you do?

options.text: Drive closely behind the emergency vehicle.
Drive as fast as the emergency vehicle.
Stay at least 500 feet behind the emergency vehicle.
Drive very slowly near the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at least 500 feet behind the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: After an emergency vehicle passes, you must stay at least 500 feet behind it.

questions.question: Before you start your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start your vehicle, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What should you do after a train passes at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Look for other approaching trains and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for other approaching trains and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: Even if only one train has passed, always check for other approaching trains before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to see through the rear window when backing up. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors, as children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: What is the penalty for someone under 21 who drinks alcohol but is not driving?

options.text: A 90-day license suspension and up to a $500 fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A 90-day license suspension and up to a $500 fine.
questions.explanation: The minimum penalties for a first underage drinking offense are a fine of up to $500, plus court costs, and a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: What happens to someone under 16 who uses a fake ID to buy alcohol?

options.text: Their driving privilege is suspended starting on their 16th birthday.
They cannot take the driver's exam until they are 21.
Their driving privilege is suspended starting on their 21st birthday.
They must attend an alcohol safety class.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their driving privilege is suspended starting on their 16th birthday.
questions.explanation: Even if you are not driving, your driving privilege will be suspended if you are convicted of alcohol-related offenses. If you are under 16, the suspension starts on your 16th birthday.

questions.question: When traveling behind a motorcycle, what following distance should you allow?
questions.explanation: On dry roads, four seconds of space is a safe following distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Always leave extra space when following a motorcycle.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit posted on the sign begins right at that sign.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The beginning of a reduced speed zone.
You are more likely to see pedestrians.
The end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a reduced speed zone.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means "Yield." Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and crossing traffic go first. Only stop if you need to.

questions.question: You must use your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles from ____ feet away.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to use your headlights when you cannot see pedestrians or other vehicles on the road 1,000 feet ahead of you.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.
